notes.title: Description
notes.value: Product ui does not warn user of unsafe actions in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook. Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user. Exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

This vulnerability discloses a user's NTLMv2 hash to the attacker who could use this to authenticate as the user.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permissions to add or modify content on an affected SharePoint page could store malicious script content in the page. The script could run in the security context of another user when that user views and interacts with the affected content, potentially allowing the attacker to access or modify SharePoint data available to that user.

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Message Queuing Queue Manager allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS Metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability would rely upon complex memory shaping techniques to attempt an attack.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

notes.title: FAQ

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to an affected service over the network. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the target system. No authentication or user interaction is required.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server. User interaction is not required.

factors.applicability: Microsoft Customer Action Required: Yes. Affected Windows Server 2016 through 2025 and Windows 10/11 builds have fixes in listed updates.
factors.exploitability: AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N. Requires an authenticated low-level account but no user interaction. E:U. No public proof of concept is indicated.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates exist for the listed builds. No workaround is in the record, so patching is the primary control.
factors.technical_impact: C/I/A High. Microsoft: an authenticated attacker can execute code on the server. Vendor severity Critical with CVSS 8.8 (below 9.0 and not pre-authentication), so the critical pre-auth RCE archetype does not apply.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation 'more-likely' gives Elevated. KEV false, exploitation detected false, publicly disclosed false. EPSS null, which is missing, not zero.
factors.uncertainty: Whether the affected role is on domain controllers or other AD DS servers is not stated. The privilege of the code executed is not stated. Scheduling is Out-of-cycle, not Immediate, because pre-auth status is absent.
factors.workload_context: AD DS is the identity control plane. Code execution on a domain service concentrates trust across the forest. Customer concentration is inherent to the role and not assumed absent.

risk_communication.summary: Authenticated network code execution in Active Directory Domain Services with Microsoft More Likely exploitation. Identity-tier impact warrants out-of-cycle handling.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Critical technical severity with an Elevated threat gives Out-of-cycle. It is not Immediate because the attacker needs a valid low-privilege account and the source is not pre-authentication.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Segmentation and isolation reduce opportunity only for non-permitted peers. Domain members remain residual. Strong authentication does not help against an already valid principal. Only patching removes the flaw.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft or CISA changes the exploitation assessment or adds KEV
Public proof of concept or EPSS appears
Evidence that the flaw is reachable without an authenticated account
Confirmation that affected servers are domain controllers

tag_evidence.evidence: Product 'Active Directory Domain Services'; Microsoft description: 'Incorrect authorization in Active Directory Domain Services'.
FAQ: 'could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server'; CVSS AV:N, UI:N.
Title: 'Remote Code Execution Vulnerability'; description: 'allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network'.

attack_path.evidence: Microsoft FAQ: 'An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server. User interaction is not required.' Entry is a network request to the AD DS listener by a low-privilege authenticated principal (AV:N, PR:L, UI:N). Target privilege context of the executed code is not stated.

title: Active Directory Domain Services Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Inbound route to AD DS listeners. Assumed public-ingress removal earns ordinary one-step credit. Residual: domain-joined and internal peers and allowed origins. The advisory does not state that any domain controller is internet-facing.
Restrictive ACLs on domain-controller service ports limit non-domain network peers. Residual: domain members and the authenticated principal remain eligible.
AD DS is the required identity service on domain controllers. No optional sub-feature is named and no vendor disablement exists. Disabling the directory service is not a workable control.
MSRC notes give only update guidance. No workaround is published.
No CVE-specific signature for the race path is supplied. Zero credit.
The AD DS route is not an HTTP route established in the source.
No setting is named that removes the race prerequisite. Zero credit.
The attacker already holds a valid low-privilege principal. Authentication does not cure an authorization or race flaw exploited through that account.
PR:L is generic and names no removable privilege. SYSTEM outcome on a domain controller is not reduced by a source-grounded containment step.
The source does not establish that the chain starts an untrusted executable or script.
No mapped ASR technique is named.
No user-delivered content route is established.
No Office path is involved.
No tested prevention rule for this race condition is supplied.
Detection and response has no likelihood credit.
Recovery only. Identity compromise is not reduced by backups.
Complete isolation of domain controllers would sever legitimate domain authentication for permitted clients, and the advisory path is a valid-account network path. No marginal credit.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper authentication in Active Directory Domain Services allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

factors.applicability: Microsoft states customer action is required for AD DS on listed Windows Server and client builds.
factors.exploitability: AV:N, AC:H (race condition), PR:L, UI:N. Winning the race is required per FAQ.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates per build in MSRC table. No workaround published.
factors.technical_impact: C:H/I:H/A:H. Attacker gains SYSTEM privileges per FAQ on domain controllers or AD DS hosts.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft Exploitation More Likely, so Elevated floor. Not KEV, not exploitation detected, EPSS null.
factors.uncertainty: Vendor severity is Critical while CVSS 3.1 base is 7.5; the discrepancy is not explained in the source. Race reliability and network exposure of domain controllers are not stated.
factors.workload_context: Identity control plane: AD DS on domain controllers. Compromise has tier-0 concentration across domain members and authentication flows.

risk_communication.summary: Network race-condition EoP to SYSTEM in AD DS, rated Critical by Microsoft and More Likely to be exploited.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Critical-technical archetype with an Elevated floor. Identity-control-plane concentration supports Out-of-cycle; the AC:H race and PR:L keep it short of Immediate.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Ordinary reachability credit is at most one band and cannot stop authenticated domain principals. No vendor workaround exists.

No technique-specific ASR rule is mapped to this stack-based overflow in the source, and enforcement is not established. Zero.
Detection and response improves visibility after a user opens the workbook but earns no likelihood or consequence credit under the catalogue.
Generic EDR presence is not a tested prevention rule for this Excel exploit behavior. No exploit-specific prevention evidence is in the source. Zero.
A user-content path is supported by the FAQ, but the mail or browser channel that delivers the workbook is not stated. Filtering cannot be matched to an established content-delivery path. Zero.
The network vector passes the production gate, but no CVE-specific IPS signature is in the source and the transport carrying the file is unstated. Zero.
Impact includes A:H, but backups are recovery after execution, not containment of the technical impact. No likelihood credit. Zero.
AV:N establishes network-delivered content, but the source does not identify the transport or permitted peers an offline enclave would cut. Zero.

FAQ and description state code executes with the user's privileges. Removing standing elevated rights from that user contains the consequence. It does not reduce the user-opened initial execution, so no likelihood credit.

Excel workbook from an untrusted source is an Office path. The source does not establish that Protected View addresses the save or convert step, and no configured policy is shown. Low confidence, zero.
No setting that removes a required exploit prerequisite is stated. Zero.
Direction is outbound client delivery of user-opened content. Public-ingress removal applies only to inbound services. Zero.
Same network-path gap as isolation: no source-established restrictable entry or peer set for the workbook delivery. Zero.

The path is a user opening a file. No authentication gates the vulnerable path. Zero.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Stack-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Excel allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted workbook in an affected version of Excel and save it in a different file format. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the user's privileges.

factors.applicability: Microsoft sets Customer Action Required: Yes. Affected products are Microsoft 365 Apps, LTSC 2021 and 2024, LTSC and 365 for Mac, and Office Online Server.
factors.exploitability: UI:R. The attacker must convince a user to open a crafted workbook and save it in another format (FAQ). AC:L and PR:N. The Preview Pane is stated not to be a vector.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and release notes are listed per product. No workaround or disablement text is in the source.
factors.technical_impact: Stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121) with code execution with the user's privileges per FAQ. C:H/I:H/A:H.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitability Less Likely (Plausible floor). KEV false. Exploitation not detected. Publicly disclosed false. EPSS null. CISA ADP SSVC: exploitation none, automatable no.
factors.uncertainty: Microsoft severity is Critical while its CVSS is 8.8 (High) and CNA vendor_severity is HIGH; attributed separately. The transport for the crafted workbook is not stated. Preview Pane conclusion is Microsoft's.
factors.workload_context: Endpoint Office desktop users who open untrusted workbooks. Office Online Server is also listed; the record does not say which role is targeted. Concentration is unknown.

risk_communication.summary: Critical-severity Excel RCE needing user interaction. Microsoft rates exploitation Less Likely, with no KEV entry and no published exploitation.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Critical-technical archetype: Microsoft severity is Critical, but CVSS is 8.8 with UI:R, so the pre-auth critical RCE anchor does not apply. Plausible likelihood keeps the Out-of-cycle baseline. No verified control credit applies.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Assessed controls are not verified in this customer's environment. Email and web filtering and IPS credit are withheld because the transport is unstated. Least privilege reduces consequence only. Backups do not contain execution.
reassessment_triggers: KEV listing or Microsoft exploitation-detected update
Public proof of concept or exploit code
Microsoft or CNA revision changing the delivery channel or severity
EPSS rising to 0.01 or above

tag_evidence.evidence: Microsoft Description: 'Stack-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Excel allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.'
Microsoft FAQ: 'An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted workbook in an affected version of Excel'

reasons: Transport for the attacker-supplied workbook (mail, web, share) is not stated, so email and web filtering credit is withheld. Source question: how is the crafted workbook delivered?

CVSS AV:N and UI:R establish attacker content reaching the victim client over the network. The transport (mail, web download, share) is not stated, so no email or web channel is credited. Processing is later, inside Excel on the user's endpoint, with the user's privileges per the FAQ. The Preview Pane is stated not to be a vector. No listener is established.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: This CVE was assigned by Chrome. Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) ingests Chromium, which addresses this vulnerability. Please see Google Chrome Releases for more information.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

attack_path.evidence: CPANSec CNA: 'A cross-site HTML form can post POSTDATA' to the endpoint. The attacker-controlled page is delivered to and rendered by the victim browser (web delivery). The server-side CGI parsing is later processing and does not erase the stated client-side delivery.

cna.description:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow the POSTDATA, PUTDATA, PATCHDATA and XForms:Model parameters to be set from the query string or form fields.

CGI stores a non-form request body under POSTDATA, PUTDATA or PATCHDATA, and an XForms body under XForms:Model, but also accepts these names from the query string, a form field or a multipart part, so an application cannot tell a client-sent value from the real body.

A cross-site HTML form can post POSTDATA={"admin":true} to an endpoint that reads JSON from param('POSTDATA'), a request forgery that needs no CORS preflight.

notes.value: Improper control of generation of code ('code injection') in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Server-side request forgery (ssrf) in Azure Managed Grafana allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Why are there no links to an update or instructions with steps that must be taken to protect from this vulnerability?

This vulnerability has already been fully mitigated by Microsoft. There is no action for users of this service to take. The purpose of this CVE is to provide further transparency.

Please see Toward greater transparency: Unveiling Cloud Service CVEs for more information.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could cause the affected service to send a request to a system they control, disclosing a service access token. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to act with the permissions granted to that token. No user interaction is required.

title: Windows Function Discovery SSDP Provider Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The route is explicitly adjacent-only. Public-ingress removal gives no benefit to adjacent routes. Zero.

Restrictive ACLs limit which adjacent peers can send discovery traffic to the SSDP provider. Residual: permitted segment peers and any compromised peer. The AC:H allocation-failure condition is not removed.

The Function Discovery SSDP Provider is a listening service that processes device information, so it is a named request-handling operation. Disabling it removes the operation for ordinary benefit. No vendor disablement text, so no path block.
No vendor workaround in the record. Zero.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Use after free in Windows Function Discovery SSDP Provider allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over an adjacent network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires an allocation to fail while the affected service processes device information. This additional condition makes an attack more difficult to trigger reliably.

factors.applicability: Microsoft states customer action is required. Updates are listed for Windows 10, 11 and Server 2016 to 2025 builds.
factors.exploitability: AV:A, AC:H, PR:N, UI:N. The attacker must trigger an allocation failure while the service processes device information.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates exist. No workaround is listed.
factors.technical_impact: C, I and A are all High. Microsoft describes unauthorized code execution over an adjacent network.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation assessment less-likely (Plausible floor). KEV false, exploitation not detected, publicly disclosed false, E:U, EPSS null.
factors.uncertainty: The adjacent message path to the SSDP provider is not described, so segmentation credit depends on it. Vendor severity is Critical, but CVSS 7.5 and AV:A do not meet the pre-auth network RCE archetype.
factors.workload_context: Windows endpoints and servers with the SSDP provider running. Adjacent-segment hosts concentrate exposure. Customer concentration is not assumed.

risk_communication.summary: Unauthenticated adjacent-network attackers can execute code through a use-after-free in SSDP provider processing, under a high-complexity allocation-failure condition.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Microsoft Critical severity with code execution routes to Out-of-cycle, not Immediate. The CVSS is 7.5, the vector is adjacent and the complexity is High, and the likelihood is Plausible.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Public-ingress removal does not apply. Segmentation and disabling the service are ordinary credits. Permitted segment peers remain residual.
reassessment_triggers: Exploitation or public exploit evidence appears
Microsoft changes the AC rating or the vector
EPSS reaches 0.01 or above

notes.value: Use after free in Windows Function Discovery Resource Publication allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over an adjacent network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker on the same network segment could send specially crafted SOAP requests to a system running the Function Discovery Resource Publication service. Exploitation depends on inducing a low-memory allocation failure and winning an asynchronous request-cleanup timing condition. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code as SYSTEM.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires the target system to be under sustained low-memory (memory pressure) conditions, which are not commonly present in normal operation. This makes the vulnerability difficult to reliably trigger, as the attacker must first induce or wait for a constrained memory state before exploitation becomes possible.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Access allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could provide a specially crafted database and convince a user to open it in Microsoft Access and drag an object from the database to another application. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the user's permissions. The attacker does not need an account on the affected system.

factors.technical_impact: CVSS C:H/I:H/A:H with code executed with the user's permissions. Not local SYSTEM.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitability less-likely (Plausible floor). KEV false; exploitation_detected false; publicly_disclosed false; EPSS null (missing, not zero); CISA ADP SSVC exploitation none.
factors.uncertainty: Scheduled was challenged: execution is at user level, not SYSTEM, and no shared secret or cross-user path is stated. The unstated delivery channel and Protected View policy coverage are unresolved.
factors.workload_context: Microsoft Access desktop database on Office 365 endpoints. The source does not state shared-database or deployment concentration.

risk_communication.summary: Important heap-overflow RCE in Access triggered by a crafted database opened by a user and dragged to another application. Code runs with that user's permissions.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Standard-remediation baseline with Plausible likelihood (Microsoft less-likely, no KEV, no EPSS), giving Scheduled. The challenge against local SYSTEM, shared secrets and cross-user access did not show a higher impact basis in the source.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with Site Member permissions on an affected SharePoint site could send a specially crafted request over the network. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the affected SharePoint server. No user interaction is required.

notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires the Allow PNG as a graphics format setting to be enabled in Word's Web Options and a user to save a specially crafted document as a web page. This export configuration is outside the attacker's direct control.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

factors.applicability: MSRC states Customer Action Required Yes for the Office Word builds listed by product ID, including 365 Apps and LTSC 2021/2024 and Mac builds. There is no no-action statement.
factors.exploitability: AC:H. Exploitation requires Allow PNG as a graphics format in Word Web Options and a user saving a crafted document as a web page. MSRC says this export is outside the attacker's control. No delivery channel is stated.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and release notes per product ID. No Microsoft workaround text; the PNG setting is a prerequisite, not a documented fix.
factors.technical_impact: CWE-121 stack buffer overflow with C/I/A High per the copied CVSS. Microsoft says code execution over a network; no execution privilege is stated for this CVE.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation assessment Less Likely, which sets the Plausible floor. KEV false. Exploitation not detected. Publicly disclosed false, which does not prove no public exploit exists. EPSS null. CISA-ADP SSVC exploitation none, automatable no.
factors.uncertainty: The delivery route for the crafted document, the default state of the PNG setting, and whether code runs only as the user are unstated. The normalized AV:N differs from the local document-input entry.
factors.workload_context: Office Word on endpoints. The taxonomy has no Office-specific workload tag. Concentration on shared document paths is unknown.

risk_communication.summary: Important Office Word RCE with user interaction, a Less Likely Microsoft assessment, no KEV and no EPSS. Scheduled on the normal cycle.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Standard-remediation archetype: Important severity with Plausible likelihood. It is not Elevated and not a pre-auth network RCE. Scheduled was challenged against local-to-SYSTEM, shared secrets and cross-user access: none is stated, the code runs in user context, and identity or storage concentration is unknown.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Only protocol hardening and Protected View carry credit, both as a single step. Email and web filtering have no established delivery route. EDR and backups give no likelihood credit.

EPSS at or above 0.01 or 0.10
Public proof of concept or exploit publication
Confirmed delivery route by mail or web
Microsoft revising customer action or the PNG prerequisite

MSRC FAQ: 'save a specially crafted document as a web page'. The attacker content is a document the user must open or export.

reasons: MSRC does not state how the crafted document reaches the user (mail, web or share). Is there an established mail or browser delivery route for email/web filtering?
The normalized AV:N conflicts with the established local document-input entry. Is any remote delivery step stated by Microsoft?
Is the Allow PNG as a graphics format setting enabled by default in customer configurations? This is not stated.

attack_path.evidence: MSRC FAQ: an attacker provides a specially crafted Word document and the victim must save it as a web page with Allow PNG as a graphics format enabled in Web Options. No mail, web or share transport is stated, so the established entry is local document input, not a listener. Record AV:N and AC:H are kept as copied.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could provide a specially crafted Word document and convince a user to open it, enable editing, and apply a sharpening correction to an embedded picture. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the user's permissions. The attacker does not need an account on the affected system.

factors.workload_context: Office desktop application on endpoints, running in user context. Enterprise concentration of Office endpoints is broad. Local-to-SYSTEM, shared-secret and cross-user concentration are not established by the source.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could host a malicious server and convince a user to connect to it from an affected client. When the client processes the server's response, the attacker could execute code on the client system. User interaction is required.

factors.applicability: MSRC states Customer Action Required Yes. Windows 10/11 client and Windows Server 2012 to 2025 builds are listed by product ID, with a KB per product.
factors.exploitability: AC:L and UI:R. The attacker hosts a malicious server, the victim client connects to it, and the client processes the response. No account is needed.

factors.technical_impact: CWE-822 untrusted pointer dereference. Microsoft says code can run on the client system. C/I/A High. Execution context is not stated.

factors.uncertainty: The 'Role: DNS Server' note conflicts with the client-side FAQ. The CNA cpe and affected lists are not fully aligned on some builds. Whether a DNS server-role host can be the victim is unresolved.
factors.workload_context: dns, from the title component. Applies to Windows clients and servers. The DNS infrastructure concentration is unknown and is the main Scheduled challenge: if DNS servers are in scope, impact is wider.

risk_communication.summary: Important Windows DNS client-side RCE that needs user connection to an attacker server. Scheduled on the normal cycle, with segmentation credit for outbound ACLs.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who controls a replication peer could supply specially crafted data over an existing replication connection. Processing that data could allow code execution in the affected replication process. The attacker does not need an account on the target server, and no additional user interaction is required during normal replication.

Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation requires the affected SQL Server instance to have the vulnerable replication feature and topology configured. An attacker with access to a participating database or replication peer cannot enable this server configuration through the vulnerability.

notes.value:
Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation requires the affected SQL Server instance to have the vulnerable replication feature and topology configured. An attacker with access to a participating database or replication peer cannot enable this server configuration through the vulnerability.

factors.applicability: Microsoft states customer action is required. November 2026 GDR and CU updates are listed for the SQL Server 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2025 x64 branches.
factors.exploitability: AC:H: the replication feature and topology must be configured, and the attacker cannot enable them through this bug. PR:L: a valid authorized database account is needed. UI:N.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates exist (GDR/CU). The record lists no vendor workaround. Patching is the primary remedy.
factors.technical_impact: C, I and A are all High. The CNA says the flaw elevates privileges over a network. The FAQ says the attacker could run SQL code with elevated privileges.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation assessment less-likely (Plausible floor). KEV false, exploitation not detected, publicly disclosed false, E:U, EPSS null. CISA-ADP SSVC lists exploitation none; this is attributed ADP evidence and does not override Microsoft.
factors.uncertainty: Whether any customer runs the replication topology is unknown. Scheduled is challenged by database concentration and sysadmin-level impact, but AC:H, PR:L and Plausible likelihood support Scheduled.
factors.workload_context: SQL Server database workload on server deployments. Shared database and replication peers concentrate impact. Customer concentration is not assumed.

risk_communication.summary: Authorized database users can elevate privileges over the network in SQL Server when replication is configured. Microsoft says a patch is required.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The Important severity, Plausible likelihood and AC:H with PR:L and a replication prerequisite support Scheduled. Database concentration and sysadmin-level impact were challenged, but the prerequisites keep the baseline at Scheduled.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Credits are ordinary only. Disabling replication has operational cost and is not vendor-verified. Authorized internal peers and replication peers remain residual. Detection gives no likelihood credit.

notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level access could send a specially crafted request to an affected service. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute database commands with elevated privileges.

factors.applicability: Microsoft Customer Action Required: Yes. Listed SQL Server 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2025 GDR and CU branches each have a November 2026 update.
factors.exploitability: AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N. Requires an authenticated low-privilege SQL login. Microsoft E:U. No public proof of concept is indicated.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates exist for every listed branch. No vendor workaround is in the record, so patching is the primary control.
factors.technical_impact: C/I/A High. Microsoft: successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute database commands with elevated privileges (SQL sysadmin-level impact per the product description).
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation 'less-likely' gives the Plausible floor. KEV false, exploitation detected false, publicly disclosed false. EPSS is null, which is missing data, not a score of zero, so it does not lower the assessment.
factors.uncertainty: EPSS not provided. Which logins are low-privilege, and whether the listener is reachable beyond internal peers, is not stated. Scheduled challenge: sysadmin escalation gives cross-database (cross-user) access on the instance, and database-tier concentration is not assumed absent. Scheduled is retained because PR:L and Microsoft's less-likely rating outweigh that concentration. Prioritise instances that hold many tenant databases.
factors.workload_context: Database tier. Sysadmin on one instance reaches every database on it. Credentials and data stored there are shared across users. Customer concentration is unknown and not assumed.

risk_communication.summary: Network-reachable SQL injection elevation to sysadmin, requiring a valid low-privilege login. Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, with no KEV entry and no EPSS.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Standard remediation is Scheduled. The Plausible likelihood and PR:L prerequisite outweigh the database concentration; the concentration argues for patching the database tier early within the cycle rather than deferring.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Network reachability controls reduce opportunity only for non-permitted peers. Permitted application and admin logins remain residual. Detection and backups do not lower likelihood. Only patching removes the flaw.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft or CISA changes the exploitation assessment or adds KEV
An EPSS score or public proof of concept appears
Evidence that the affected instances host multi-tenant databases or are reachable from untrusted networks
Microsoft adds a workaround or changes the required privilege

Entry is a network request to the SQL Server listener made by a valid low-privilege principal (PR:L, AV:N, UI:N). The record does not state the login scope, the listener exposure, or the request protocol. Later processing is the SQL command path that runs database commands with elevated privileges.

An authenticated attacker with permission to create or modify database objects could prepare specially crafted content in an affected database. factors.applicability: Microsoft states Customer Action Required: Yes for listed SQL Server GDR and CU branches. Advisory applicability is clear.
factors.exploitability: Attacker needs an authenticated DB account with object create/modify permission (PR:L) and an administrator must run the processing operation (UI:R). Both preconditions reduce practical reliability.
factors.remediation_context: Updates 5129299, 5132751, 5132747, 5132749, 5132745, 5132748 and 5132746 are listed by product branch. No workaround is published.
factors.technical_impact: CVSS C:H/I:H/A:H with an elevation-of-privilege impact that runs database commands with elevated privileges. The impact is database-wide if the admin context is high.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation assessment is less-likely, so the published likelihood maps to Plausible. KEV false, exploitation detected false, publicly disclosed false, EPSS null (not provided). CISA-ADP SSVC exploitation none is a separate attributed fact.
factors.uncertainty: The admin operation, its runtime privilege context, and the DB client protocol are not described. EPSS is absent. Microsoft's publication does not establish that no public proof of concept exists.
factors.workload_context: SQL Server is a shared database service, so cross-user access within the database is a concentration concern. Customer deployment concentration is unknown and is not assumed.

risk_communication.summary: Important SQL Server EoP with Microsoft less-likely exploitation. Standard scheduled remediation applies, with network-route and privilege-removal credit recorded as what-if evidence.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Scheduled follows the standard-remediation archetype: CVSS 8.0, PR:L, UI:R, and Microsoft less-likely with no KEV or EPSS evidence. I challenged the Scheduled timing: the impact is database-wide and crosses users, but the attacker needs a valid DB account and a separate admin must act, so I did not escalate.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Network-route controls cover only the established listener path and leave authorized clients residual. Removing object-permission grants from the attacker's principal does not stop other principals who hold them. No vendor workaround exists, and EDR or backups do not lower likelihood.

reasons: Source does not describe the separate administrator operation that processes the crafted content or the privilege context it runs under, which controls consequence.

attack_path.evidence: MSRC FAQ: an authenticated attacker with permission to create or modify database objects prepares specially crafted content in an affected database; a separate administrator performs the affected administrative operation that processes it. Description and CVSS AV:N say the elevation is over a network. Entry is an authenticated network session to the SQL Server listener; the admin operation is a later processing step with UI:R. I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SQL sysadmin privileges.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation requires the affected SQL Server instance to have the vulnerable replication feature and topology configured. An attacker with access to a participating database or replication peer cannot enable this server configuration through the vulnerability.

factors.applicability: Microsoft Customer Action Required: Yes. Affected builds are SQL Server 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2025 GDR/CU lines, with fixes in the November 2026 updates.
factors.exploitability: AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N. AC:H because the vulnerable replication feature and topology must be configured. E:U. No public proof of concept is indicated.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates exist for the listed branches. No vendor workaround is given, although disabling replication where unused is a feature-level what-if.
factors.technical_impact: C/I/A High. Microsoft FAQ: an attacker could gain SQL sysadmin privileges.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation 'less-likely' gives the Plausible floor. KEV false, exploitation detected false, publicly disclosed false. EPSS null, which is missing, not zero.
factors.uncertainty: The network position needed to reach the replicating instance is not stated. Replication role and topology details are not stated beyond the FAQ. EPSS not provided. Scheduled challenge: sysadmin gives cross-database access on the instance, and replication topologies spread that exposure across peers. Customer concentration is not assumed absent.
factors.workload_context: Database tier with replication. Sysadmin on one node can affect replicated peers and their data. Customer concentration unknown.

risk_communication.summary: Network SQL elevation to sysadmin that requires a replication topology and a valid low-privilege principal. AC:H and a less-likely Microsoft rating make it a Scheduled item, with replicated database tiers as the concentration to watch.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Standard remediation is Scheduled. Replication prerequisites and the less-likely rating outweigh the sysadmin and replicated-peer concentration, so the item is handled in the cycle.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Disabling replication is credited only as a feature what-if and only where replication is genuinely unused. Network controls reduce opportunity only for non-permitted peers. Only patching removes the flaw.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft or CISA changes the exploitation assessment or adds KEV
Public proof of concept or EPSS appears
Confirmation that replication is used on internet-reachable or multi-tenant instances
Clarification of the network position the attacker needs

tag_evidence.evidence: Affected products are Microsoft SQL Server 2017/2019/2022/2025; FAQ references the SQL Server instance replication topology.
CVSS AV:N, UI:N; description 'allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network'.
FAQ: 'could gain SQL sysadmin privileges'.

reasons: The record does not say which replication role or network position an attacker needs to reach the replicating instance.
The record does not state the replication configuration details beyond the feature and topology requirement, so AC:H credit is not further confirmed.

attack_path.evidence: Microsoft description: 'authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network' (AV:N, PR:L). FAQ and AC:H rationale: the instance must have the vulnerable replication feature and topology configured, and an attacker with access to a replication peer cannot enable it through the flaw. The request channel and the attacker's replication role are not stated. Entry is treated as a network request to the replicating SQL Server listener.

ACLs on the SQL Server listener restrict the network peers that can start the authenticated session used for the injection. Permitted DB clients remain residual.
No vendor disablement of a named feature is given. The admin operation that triggers the injected statement is not identified as a removable feature. Zero.
MSRC record has update links only, with no workaround. Zero.
No CVE-specific SQL injection signature for this record is established. Generic IPS presence earns no credit.
Transport carrying the injected SQL is not described as HTTP, so WAF route coverage and a tested rule are not established. Zero.
No setting is stated that directly removes the injection prerequisite. Zero.
The attacker is already an authenticated DB user. Strong authentication does not cure injection by a valid account. Zero.

Named required privilege: permission to create or modify database objects. Removing it from the attacker principal removes the content-creation step. Other holders remain residual. No consequence credit, since the admin context is unknown.
Injected SQL is not an untrusted executable or script dependency. Zero.
No endpoint ASR technique maps to SQL statement injection. Zero.
Injection is carried through the database, not user-delivered mail or web content.
No Office document path is described.
No tested endpoint prevention rule for SQL injection behaviour is established. Generic EDR presence gets no credit.
Detection and response only. No likelihood credit.
Recovery control. The impact is privilege elevation, not availability loss, so no consequence credit.
Full isolation of the authenticated SQL route is not established. It overlaps the public-ingress and ACL credit on the same route. Zero.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permission to create or modify database objects could prepare specially crafted content in an affected database. A separate administrator must perform the affected administrative operation that processes this content. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to run database commands with elevated privileges.

factors.applicability: Customer Action Required: Yes for listed SQL Server 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2025 GDR and CU branches.
factors.exploitability: Needs an authenticated attacker with DB object create/modify permission (PR:L), and an administrator must run the operation that executes the injected statement (UI:R).
factors.remediation_context: Branch-specific GDR and CU updates are listed. No workaround is published.
factors.technical_impact: SQL injection in an admin-executed path. CVSS C:H/I:H/A:H with elevation to running database commands with elevated privileges.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation assessment less-likely maps to Plausible. KEV false, exploitation detected false, publicly disclosed false, EPSS null.
factors.uncertainty: The injection sink, the admin operation, and the privilege context are not described. EPSS is absent. The advisory does not establish the absence of exploit code.
factors.workload_context: Shared SQL Server database. Cross-user access inside the database is a concentration concern. Customer deployment concentration is unknown.

risk_communication.summary: Important CWE-89 SQL injection EoP with Microsoft less-likely exploitation, requiring an authenticated DB user and an admin-run operation. Scheduled remediation applies.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Standard-remediation archetype: CVSS 8.0 with PR:L and UI:R, and Microsoft less-likely. I challenged Scheduled because cross-user database access is high-impact, but the injection sink needs an authenticated attacker and an admin action, so escalation is not supported by the evidence.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Network credit covers the established listener route only, and authorized clients remain residual. Least-privilege credit applies to the named object-permission step only. No workaround exists. Detection does not reduce likelihood.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft or CISA changes exploitation status or publishes KEV or EPSS
The injection sink or the admin operation's privilege context is published
A public exploit or workaround appears

tag_evidence.evidence: MSRC FAQ: authenticated attacker with permission to create or modify database objects in an affected database; product Microsoft SQL Server.
MSRC description: SQL injection allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network; FAQ: run database commands with elevated privileges.

reasons: Source does not identify the statement or sink that the admin operation executes, nor its privilege context, which determines consequence.
Source does not identify the transport for the authenticated session, so route-level WAF credit cannot be established.

attack_path.evidence: MSRC CWE-89 description: SQL injection allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network. FAQ: an authenticated attacker with DB object create/modify permission prepares crafted content; a separate administrator performs the operation that processes it. Entry is an authenticated network session to SQL Server. The injected SQL executes later in the admin operation's processing (UI:R). Gap: the statement executed by the admin operation and its privilege context are not described.

Local-to-SYSTEM and shared secrets are not stated. Concentration of shared database instances is unknown. Admin and authentication prerequisites support Scheduled.

risk_communication.summary: Important SQL Server elevation-of-privilege through admin-processed database content. Threat is Plausible; action is Scheduled.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Standard-remediation archetype: not Critical and Plausible likelihood. Two conditions (authenticated object-permission holder and separate admin action) support Scheduled after the cross-user challenge.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permission to synchronize a database subscription could send a specially crafted request to an affected SQL Server instance. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute database commands beyond the intended replication functionality. No user interaction is required.

notes.value: Improper authentication in ASP.NET Core allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a password reset request using a specially crafted email address that is treated as equivalent to another account. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to take over the targeted account. No user interaction is required.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

factors.applicability: Microsoft marks Customer Action Required Yes for Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). Remediation is a Security Update and Release Notes. The source says the latest Edge build is no longer vulnerable, so the update must be installed.
factors.exploitability: CVSS AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R. The Chrome CNA says the attacker had already compromised the renderer process and used crafted network traffic. Exploitation therefore needs a renderer compromise the record does not establish, plus user interaction. ADP SSVC lists exploitation none and automatable no.
factors.remediation_context: Edge update is the source-stated fix. No vendor workaround is published. Installed-version status is unknown in this record.
factors.technical_impact: Microsoft gives C:H/I:H/A:H. The Chrome CNA states arbitrary code execution outside the sandbox. ADP SSVC gives technical impact total. The impact is high on endpoints but depends on the chained renderer compromise.
factors.threat_evidence: No KEV entry. exploitation_detected false, but exploitation_assessment unknown and no Microsoft Exploitability Index is published, so the likelihood floor is Plausible. publicly_disclosed is null. EPSS is 0.00223, below the 0.01 raise threshold. The CNA and ADP do not show exploitation.
factors.uncertainty: Renderer compromise is an assumed precondition not established by this record. Microsoft exploitation assessment and public-disclosure state are unknown. The Microsoft (Important) and Chrome (High) severity labels are on different scales and both are retained. Installed build status is unknown.
factors.workload_context: Endpoint Chromium browser population. Fleet size and whether browsers run under privileged accounts are unknown in this record, so concentration is not assumed.

risk_communication.summary: Important, CVSS 8.8 browser sandbox-escape chain. Microsoft requires customer action to install the fixed Edge build. Threat evidence is Plausible with no KEV, no detected exploitation and EPSS 0.00223. Baseline action is Scheduled under the standard-remediation archetype.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The archetype is standard-remediation because the CVSS is below 9.0 and threat is not Elevated. The source has UI:R, a renderer-compromise prerequisite, no exploitation signal and CNA SSVC automatable no, so no higher action is supported. The impact is high on endpoints, so Scheduled is challenged. Browser updates are routinely deployed and no shared-secret or cross-user concentration is established, so the action stays at Scheduled.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Email/web filtering is credited one likelihood step only, with no exact block, because no malicious URL or signature is published. It cannot address the assumed renderer-compromise foothold, admitted content or compromised destinations. Detection and response adds no credit. Least privilege and segmentation have no source-established credit.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft or CISA adds the CVE to KEV or reports exploitation detected.
Microsoft publishes an Exploitability Index rating of More Likely or a public proof of concept appears.
EPSS reaches 0.01 or higher.
The renderer-compromise precondition is shown to be publicly chained with this CVE.
Microsoft changes customer-action or remediation text.
Fleet data shows Edge builds remaining on affected versions in privileged or shared contexts.

tag_evidence.evidence: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) affected product with CVSS UI:R; Chrome CNA crafted network traffic from a remote attacker to the browser.
Microsoft CVSS UI:R requires user interaction to render attacker-controlled content in the browser; Chrome CNA crafted network traffic.
Chrome CNA description: allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox.

reasons: Renderer compromise is an assumed precondition in the Chrome CNA text and is not established by this record. Which earlier foothold is used in practice is unknown.
Microsoft exploitation assessment is unknown and no Exploitability Index is published, so the Plausible floor depends on missing evidence.
Microsoft (Important) and Chrome (High) severity labels are on different scales; confirm the Microsoft rating governs.

attack_path.evidence: Microsoft (publisher) product is Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) with CVSS AV:N and UI:R, so the entry is victim-client browser delivery of attacker-controlled web content. The Chrome CNA (assigning CNA, not Microsoft) describes exploitation by a remote attacker via crafted network traffic. That CNA text states the attacker had already compromised the renderer process, so a renderer compromise is an assumed earlier foothold that this record does not establish. No controls are credited against that earlier foothold. The current CVE is the Quota reference-resolution flaw that escapes the sandbox after renderer compromise, and the CNA says the escape yields arbitrary code execution outside the sandbox. ADP CISA SSVC lists exploitation none and automatable no.

cna.description: Incorrect reference resolution in Quota in Google Chrome prior to 156.0.8078.79 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via crafted network traffic. (Chromium security severity: High)

This is a Chromium browser issue. No Office content path exists.
No documented setting removes the Quota reference-resolution prerequisite. Release Notes are not mitigation text.

Rendering the page is a required browser operation. No vendor disablement of a feature is stated.
No authentication gate is stated on the crafted-page path.
Microsoft's guidance is the Edge security update. No CVE-specific workaround text is given.
The route to the renderer is unknown. WAF credit requires a tested blocking rule on an inbound route, and none is established.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that might include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, low privileges are required (PR:L). What privileges are required?

An attacker must have an authenticated SharePoint account with permission to add content and personalize an existing page. Farm administrator permissions are not required.

factors.applicability: Customer Action Required Yes. Product is Microsoft SharePoint Server Subscription Edition (x64), remediated by Security Update 5002945 and support article. Affected below 16.0.20326.20278.

CISA-ADP SSVC exploitation none and automatable no, separately attributed and not used to override Microsoft.
factors.workload_context: SharePoint is a web application server with a shared-service farm role. Cross-user concentration is real: a contributor-level account on a shared farm can reach server code. Farm count, content owners and identity integration are unknown.
factors.uncertainty: Code execution privilege context, the affected farm's permission model and EPSS are unknown. No public exploit maturity is published by Microsoft.

risk_communication.summary: Important SharePoint RCE that requires a low-privilege authenticated contributor account and high attack complexity. Plausible threat evidence and no KEV. Standard Scheduled remediation with the Microsoft update as the control, challenged against shared-farm impact.

These are balanced by AC:H, the authenticated permission requirement, Microsoft Less Likely and no KEV, so Scheduled holds.

attack_path.evidence: CPANSec CNA: a POST Content-Type header with multipart/related is parsed by CGI.pm, and 'No request body is needed'. The attacker sends an HTTP request to a listening CGI-based web service with no user action, which is an inbound route.

cna.description:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via a backtracking regex on the XForms multipart/related Content-Type.

When a POST Content-Type contains multipart/related, the boundary and start parameters are extracted with an unanchored pattern that puts .+ on either side of the boundary capture, which backtracks in cubic time on a header that does not match. No request body is needed.

attack_path.evidence: CNA (CPANSec): 'A client can keep a server process spinning with one such request.' The attacker sends a short-body request to a CGI application. The vulnerable path (read_postdata_putdata) is reached only when $CGI::PUTDATA_UPLOAD or an upload hook is set and $CGI::DISABLE_UPLOADS is set. Those are named configuration prerequisites, not an optional attacker route.

cna.description:
CGI versions before 5.00 for Perl allow an infinite loop on a short request body when $DISABLE_UPLOADS is set.

When $CGI::PUTDATA_UPLOAD or an upload hook is set, read_postdata_putdata takes a request body that is not a form submission. With $CGI::DISABLE_UPLOADS set, it discards the body by reading until Content-Length bytes have arrived. Once a body shorter than its Content-Length runs out, every read returns 0, so the loop never ends.

A client can keep a server process spinning with one such request.
problem_types: CWE-835 Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Exploit runs as in-process code from a crafted HTML page (CNA). The source does not show the chain starting an untrusted executable or script, so application control has no matching mechanism.
No technique-specific ASR rule is named for V8 type confusion in the Microsoft or CNA record. No credit.
Detection and response improves confidence only and gives no likelihood credit by catalogue rule.
No tested exploit-specific prevention rule for V8 type confusion is established. Generic EDR presence gives no credit.

The established route is browser web delivery of a crafted HTML page (CNA), which is user-delivered content. Assuming verified restriction of that browser content path gives one ordinary step. Residual: any permitted or compromised site, and no exploit recognition is assumed. Not an exact block.
Outbound browser traffic is applicable, but no CVE-specific or exploit-specific signature is in the source. Generic IPS presence gives no credit.
Backups are recovery only. They give no likelihood credit and no source-grounded containment of the sandbox-internal code execution.
No isolation boundary for the browsing scope is established. The delivery is ordinary web reachability, so no bounded isolation credit is claimed.
Exploit prerequisites are PR:N, so no removable named privilege is required. No source-grounded post-exploit containment is stated, so consequence credit is zero.
The vulnerable component is the Chromium browser renderer, not an Office document path. Office Protected View does not apply.
No setting is named that removes the V8 type-confusion prerequisite. Rendering HTML is the core browser function, so no credit.
Outbound victim-client delivery. Public-ingress removal gives no benefit, since the attacker is a server the victim connects to.

Restrictive egress ACLs limiting browser-reachable destinations to a permitted set restrict the attacker-hosted page path. Residual: permitted destinations and any admitted attacker-hosted or compromised site remain. One ordinary step only.
No vendor disablement guidance is published for this CVE. Microsoft and CNA text give only the fixed Chromium version.
PR:N and no authentication gate on the path. Authentication cannot restrict a victim browsing to a crafted page.
No CVE-specific vendor workaround is published. The remediation is updating Edge to the Chromium release that fixes the issue (CNA: prior to 157.0.8103.38).
WAF inspects inbound requests to a protected service. This is outbound browser rendering of attacker content.

Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

factors.applicability: Microsoft marks Customer Action Required Yes for Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based), product 22414. The fix is the Chromium update to 157.0.8103.38 or later.
factors.exploitability: CVSS 8.8 with AV:N, AC:L, PR:N, UI:R. Entry needs the victim to load an attacker HTML page. V8 type confusion is the processing step, with arbitrary code inside the sandbox.
factors.remediation_context: Update to the fixed Edge release. No vendor workaround or disablement is published. Email/web filtering and egress ACL credit are one-step each, not exact blocks.
factors.technical_impact: Confidentiality, integrity and availability are High, with scope unchanged. CNA says arbitrary code runs inside the sandbox, so the RCE tag is kept.
factors.threat_evidence: KEV false. Microsoft exploitation assessment unknown and not published, so the floor is Plausible pending evidence. EPSS 0.00403 is below 0.01, so no raise. CISA-ADP SSVC gives exploitation none.
factors.uncertainty: No Microsoft exploitability index or public exploit status is published. Sandbox-internal impact is stated, not sandbox-escape. Patched state of any given installation is not known from this record.
factors.workload_context: Browser endpoint in user context. No Windows server or identity workload is named. Browser deployment breadth is not known from this record.

risk_communication.summary: Important Edge (Chromium) V8 type confusion, CVSS 8.8, user interaction required. No KEV, no exploitation detected, EPSS 0.00403. Standard remediation: update Edge to the fixed Chromium release on the normal Scheduled cadence.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Not Critical and not Important with Elevated likelihood, so it falls to standard remediation. Likelihood is Plausible because Microsoft has not published exploitability. The user-interaction requirement and absence of exploitation evidence keep Scheduled.

Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

factors.applicability: Microsoft marks Customer Action Required Yes for Edge (Chromium-based), product 22414. The fix is the Chromium update to 157.0.8103.38 or later.
factors.exploitability: CVSS 8.3 with AC:H, UI:R and scope changed. The advisory assumes a prior renderer compromise, then sandbox escape via Skia out-of-bounds read.
factors.remediation_context: Update to the fixed Edge release. No vendor workaround is published. Filtering and egress ACL credit are one-step each.
factors.technical_impact: C/I/A High with scope changed. CNA states code execution outside the sandbox, so RCE and elevation of privilege are kept.
factors.threat_evidence: KEV false. Microsoft exploitability not published (floor Plausible). EPSS 0.00296 is below 0.01. CISA-ADP SSVC exploitation none.
factors.uncertainty: Renderer-compromise step is assumed and its transport is not separately specified. Sandbox-escape exploitability and public status are not published.
factors.workload_context: Browser endpoint in user context. No server or identity workload named.

risk_communication.summary: Important Edge (Chromium) Skia out-of-bounds read with a sandbox-escape claim, CVSS 8.3. Renderer compromise is assumed. Standard remediation: update Edge on the Scheduled cadence.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Important severity without Elevated likelihood means standard remediation. Plausible likelihood, no KEV, and a high-complexity, user-interaction chain keep Scheduled.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Filtering and egress ACL credit are one-step only and cannot block the assumed renderer compromise path precisely. The update is the only fix.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft publishes exploitability More Likely or exploitation Detected
CISA adds the CVE to KEV
EPSS reaches 0.01 or higher
A public exploit for the sandbox escape appears
Source clarifies the renderer compromise transport

tag_evidence.evidence: CNA: 'remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox'. Sandbox escape gains privilege beyond the renderer.
CNA: 'to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page'.
CNA: 'via a crafted HTML page', rendered by the victim.
CNA: 'via a crafted HTML page' delivered by web browsing.

reasons: Renderer-compromise prerequisite is assumed; its own delivery transport is not separately specified beyond the crafted HTML page.
Sandbox-escape exploitability and public exploit status are not published, so the likelihood floor relies on Microsoft not-published handling.

attack_path.evidence: CNA says a remote attacker who had already compromised the renderer process executes code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. The stated route is web delivery of the HTML page (outbound). The renderer compromise is an advisory-assumed prerequisite whose transport is not separately specified. Sandbox-escape processing in Skia is later processing. Review is required for the assumed renderer step. No listener is implied.

cna.description: Out of bounds read in Skia in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.38 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

title: Chromium CVE-2026-121087: Improper input validation

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Chain begins with HTML rendered in the browser, not an untrusted executable or script file launched by the user. No credit.
No enforced ASR rule is mapped in source to the Mobile input-validation technique. Generic ASR presence gives no credit.
Detection and response improves confidence only and gives no likelihood credit for the origin-policy bypass.
No tested prevention rule for origin-policy bypass in Mobile input validation is named. Generic EDR gives no credit.

The attacker HTML page is a user-delivered web route. Web content filtering that restricts browser delivery may remove one band of attacker-page reach. It is not exploit recognition. Residual: permitted or compromised destinations and admitted pages remain.
No CVE-specific or exploit-specific signature is cited for the crafted HTML route. No credit.
Backups do not address origin-policy bypass; no availability impact is stated as the CVE effect. No credit.
Browsing must remain reachable for the victim and the attacker page reaches the client. No source-established isolation of this entry. No credit.
Source names no removable privilege for the origin-policy bypass and no grounded post-exploit containment. No consequence credit.
No Office document path. Protected View does not act on a crafted HTML page.
No configuration setting named in sources removes the crafted-page prerequisite.
Applies only to inbound service routes. This is an outbound client receiving attacker HTML, so public-ingress removal gives no benefit.
Outbound browsing to attacker-chosen destinations is the entry. Source names no permitted-destination set, so no ACL credit; all web destinations stay residual.
Only the Mobile component is named. A bare component name is not a removable required operation and no vendor disablement is given. No credit.
No authentication gates the crafted HTML page path; the attacker needs no account.
Sources give only the update and release-note links; no CVE-specific workaround text.
Inbound-only control. The browser is not a protected inbound service for this outbound page delivery.

mitigation_candidates.evidence: No untrusted executable or script launch is established as the dependency for SVG recursion in the renderer. No credit is applied.
